items.title: For the first time, scientists watch sound jump between quantum states
items.summary: Stanford researchers have recorded the first real-time quantum jumps of sound, watching single phonons abruptly vanish from one energy state to another. items.title: Scientists create a needle-thin brain implant that can do three jobs at once
items.summary: A new needle-thin brain implant can record neural activity, deliver drugs, and stimulate multiple brain regions using a single flexible fiber. items.summary: Researchers observed a humpback whale mother staying beside her presumed stillborn calf for hours and possibly days off Australia’s Gold Coast. items.title: This new concrete is stronger and pulls CO2 from the air
items.summary: Researchers have created a concrete mixture that is both stronger and capable of absorbing carbon dioxide. items.title: A strange circle on satellite maps turned out to be a 390-million-year-old impact crater
items.summary: An amateur astronomer searching satellite maps for a Quebec camping spot accidentally discovered a massive ancient impact crater. Scientists later found shatter cones that confirmed the 25-kilometer-wide structure was blasted into Earth roughly 390 million years ago.
